title: Security review: Data residency & region pinning
summary: Medivault asked detailed questions about EU/US data residency, region pinning, cross-border processing, and sub-processor disclosure. Redwood explained hosted vs dedicated/private options, VPC/private control plane, KMS integrations, audit logging retention, and provided compliance artifacts. Agreement to share SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and schedule follow-up with legal to validate contract language for data localization and sub-processor list.
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-28 14:30 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sara Gomez (Medivault - Head InfoSec), Liam O'Connor (Cloud Architect), Anita Patel (Legal), Evan Brooks (Product)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya's our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Sara: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to go through the security questions.
[00:11] Liam: Yeah, thanks. We sent an agenda - mostly around data residency and sub-processors.
[00:16] Alex: Perfect. We'll start high-level then Priya will do the technical detail. Quick note that this is a recorded call for internal notes.

[02:05] Priya: Cool, so for the data residency ask, we support three deployment modes: hosted API (global), Dedicated (reserved capacity in a region), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For strict EU localization we recommend Dedicated or Private, where the control plane and inference are pinned to a region.

[04:10] Sara: When you say pinned to a region, do you mean both control plane and data plane stay in the EU? Any metadata leaving?
[04:18] Priya: Good question. For Dedicated we can pin inference pods to an EU region and customer data processed there. Control plane is region-aware but for Hosted the control plane is in our central region; some metadata, like billing IDs and usage metrics, may traverse the US. If you need full control, Private deployments give you a customer-managed control plane in your VPC, so nothing flows back to Redwood.

[06:55] Anita: Legally we need explicit sub-processor list. Who are your cloud providers and any third-party monitoring or logging vendors?
[07:10] Alex: Our primary infra providers are GCP and AWS depending on region; we also use Datadog for optional observability and S3-like storage for ephemeral KV cache snapshots. We can provide a current sub-processor list; we update it quarterly.

[08:30] Liam: Is there cross-border processing for Hosted? For example, if a user in France hits the API, could data be routed through US nodes for cost/latency reasons?
[08:41] Priya: For Hosted yes, global routing can move work to nearest available capacity and in peak cases fall back to other regions. For EU-only guarantees you must choose Dedicated with region pinning or Private. We also have region affinity policies to prefer EU-only for certain customers.

[11:12] Sara: On encryption—at-rest and in-flight—what's the default and what options exist for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
[11:21] Priya: All traffic is TLS1.2+ in transit; at-rest we encrypt with provider-managed keys by default. For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS; we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own HSM in Private deployments. There's a small note: for hosted multi-tenant services, keying is provider-managed unless we do a dedicated tenancy.

[13:50] Sara: Do you keep raw transcripts or customer payloads for more than X days? Residency aside, retention policy matters for GDPR.
[13:59] Alex: By default Hosted retains logs for 30 days for debugging and billing and then they are purged; Dedicated customers can configure retention and TTLs. For Private you control retention fully. We also have an option to disable data retention for inference payloads on a per-customer basis for paid tiers.

[16:20] Evan: For audit logs, do you provide immutable audit trails and what fields are included? Is there an API to stream logs to our SIEM?
[16:31] Priya: We provide request-level audit logs with timestamps, request IDs, model/version, route, and token usage metrics. We support streaming logs to your S3 or Pub/Sub and can push to Splunk/Datadog. Immutable storage can be achieved via WORM buckets on your side in Private/Dedicated setups.

[19:05] Sara: Sounds good. Legal question: do you process personal data as a processor and do you sign standard DPA with EU addendum?
[19:15] Anita: (interject) Also need SCCs if personal data crosses borders.
[19:19] Alex: Yes, we operate as a processor; we have a standard DPA that includes SCCs and an EU data processing addendum. We'll share the docs. For Private, customer is effectively hosting so the DPA reflects that model.

[22:30] Liam: About sub-processors — are there any AI model vendors or third-party inference tools that could see the data? Any open model downloaders or weight hosting outside your infra?
[22:42] Priya: We host curated open models in our catalog; model weights and runtime live on our infra. We don't send customer prompts to external model vendors. For specialized cases where a customer wants to bring their model, the model artifacts are managed by the customer in Private; we can run within your VPC.

[25:00] Sara: Regulatoryly, some of our customers want proof of ISO27001. Do you have certificates?
[25:08] Alex: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, yes. We'll attach copies of the attestation reports; redacted where necessary.

[27:40] Evan: What about employee access, RBAC and SSO—how granular is role management and can we limit support access for certain environments?
[27:50] Priya: We have role-based access controls with least privilege roles. For Dedicated we can limit Redwood support to read-only unless you explicitly grant escalation access; in Private you control access via your identity provider, SAML/OKTA, SCIM provisioning, and we can enforce MFA.

[30:12] Anita: On the contractual side, we need to see logs showing where data was processed for audit. Can Redwood provide processing locality proofs?
[30:23] Alex: We can provide region logs that show the region and node IDs handling requests. For Hosted this is aggregate; for Dedicated/Private we can produce per-request region metadata. We'll need to scope the exact format with your team.

[33:01] Liam: Performance tradeoffs—if we force EU-only routing, do we lose burst capacity? How do you handle peak loads?
[33:10] Priya: Yes, restricting to a region reduces available spare capacity; we offer burst policies and cross-region fallback options. For strict SLAs in EU we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity. We'll provide throughput numbers and historical latency percentiles for EU nodes.

[36:40] Sara: Are any sub-processors located outside EU that may process EU customer data even in Dedicated?
[36:52] Priya: For Dedicated we aim for region-local infra; however, some managed services like certain security telemetry or manage backups may be in different locations unless configured otherwise. We can list each sub-processor and region and help you choose configurations that avoid cross-border processing.

[39:15] Anita: On e-discovery and lawful requests, if a government requests data from Redwood, how is that handled for EU data?
[39:25] Alex: We follow legal process and notify customers unless prohibited. For Private deployments where data stays in your VPC, Redwood doesn't have access to data, so direct requests to Redwood don't apply. We'll provide our lawful request policy.

[42:50] Evan: A practical ask — can you provide a CSV that maps sub-processors to regions and which products use them?
[42:58] Priya: Yes, we have that and will attach it.

[45:30] Sara: Okay next steps from our side: legal will review DPA and SCCs; InfoSec may want to run a SOC2 review and a short technical audit. We may ask for a short PoC in EU region to verify latency and data flow.

[46:02] Alex: Great. From Redwood we'll: send SOC2 and ISO attestations, provide the sub-processor CSV, the region-pinning playbook, and schedule a follow-up with legal to walk through contract language. Also propose a pilot in EU Dedicated with a 2-week benchmark.

[49:20] Liam: Timeline — we need vendor approval by end of January, ideally. Can you get materials this week?

[49:28] Alex: Yes, we'll push the docs within 48 hours and propose dates for pilot.

[52:15] Anita: Minor transcription note — some of your docs refer to KV cache snapshots, can you clarify what goes into those?

[52:25] Priya: KV cache may include prefix tokens for caching; by default we don't persist customer prompts beyond retention unless configured. We'll add a short note clarifying ephemeral caches vs persistent snapshots.

[54:10] Alex: Thanks everyone. Quick recap: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO, sub-processor list CSV, region-pinning playbook, DPA with SCCs, and propose pilot dates. Medivault legal + InfoSec to review and we'll reconvene next week.
[54:38] Sara: Thanks, appreciate it.
[54:42] Alex: Thanks all, bye.
